title: Banking & Recurring Deposits: Growing Your Money

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Money That Makes Money
blocks.content: When you deposit money in a bank, the bank pays you a small reward called **interest** for letting them use your money. A **Recurring Deposit (RD)** is when you deposit a fixed amount every month (like Rs. 500/month). Over time, each deposit earns interest, and the total grows much bigger than what you put in. It's like planting seeds every month and watching a forest grow.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Simple Interest on RD
blocks.content:
For Recurring Deposits, interest is calculated using a special formula:

• **Interest = P x n(n+1) / (2 x 12) x r/100**
• P = monthly installment amount
• n = number of months
• r = annual rate of interest
• **Maturity Value = Total deposits + Interest = (P x n) + Interest**

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Calculating RD Interest
blocks.content:
Follow this process:

1. Write down P (monthly deposit), n (number of months), and r (annual rate).
2. Calculate n(n+1)/2 first. This represents the sum of months.
3. Multiply: P x [n(n+1)/2] x (1/12) x (r/100).
4. This gives you the total interest earned.
5. Add the interest to total deposits (P x n) to get the Maturity Value.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: RD Calculation
blocks.content:
Rahul deposits Rs. 500 per month for 24 months at 10% per annum.

**Step 1:** P = 500, n = 24, r = 10.
**Step 2:** n(n+1)/2 = 24 x 25 / 2 = 300.
**Step 3:** Interest = 500 x 300 x (1/12) x (10/100) = 500 x 300 x 0.00833 = Rs. 1250.
**Step 4:** Total deposited = 500 x 24 = Rs. 12,000.
**Step 5:** Maturity Value = 12,000 + 1,250 = **Rs. 13,250.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The most devastating mistake is forgetting to divide by 12! The rate 'r' is given per YEAR, but the deposits are MONTHLY. If you skip the /12 step, your interest calculation will be 12 times too large. Also, students often confuse n(n+1) with n^2. They are NOT the same! For n=24, n^2 is 576 but n(n+1) is 600.
